subject: Performance benchmarking pack + MAP deliverables / next steps
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@ai-analytics.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-04-15T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff / performance checklist

Hi Karthik —

Thanks for the quick sync earlier. Samir and I sketched an internal evaluation checklist and we want Redwood's benchmarking artifacts to slot directly into our MAP. Key asks from our infra and product teams:

- Latency p50/p95/p99 for typical production prompts (500–1k token sequences)
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT) on cold vs warm cache
- Sustained throughput (tokens/sec & requests/sec) at target concurrency (16, 64, 256)
- End-to-end concurrency behavior (tail latency under load)
- CSV exports + dashboard link for our engineers to replay plots

Can you confirm you can deliver a single asset bundle (slides + CSV + dashboard link + sample raw logs) that we can attach to the MAP by next Thursday (2026-04-22)? Also indicate the brief executive summary we can insert into the MAP.

Cheers,
Elena
Elena Torres
Head of Platform Engineering, AI Analytics
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@ai-analytics.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com, rafael.mendes@redwood.com
Date: 2026-04-15T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff / performance checklist

Elena — thanks, got it. We can absolutely produce a single "benchmark pack" that maps to the MAP line items. Proposed deliverables and timeline:

1) Benchmark pack deliverables (what you'll receive):
   - 4-page executive readout (PDF) summarizing perf/SLAs and risk areas
   - benchmark_results_summary.csv (canonical numbers used in slides)
   - raw_benchmark_logs.zip (artifact for reproducibility)
   - dashboard link with interactive p50/p95/p99 plots + concurrency heatmaps

2) Metrics we'll report (by test bucket):
   - Latency: p50 / p95 / p99 (ms) for 128/512/1024 token prompts
   - TTFT: cold start / warm cache (ms) measured from request acceptance to first token
   - Throughput: tokens/sec and requests/sec at target concurrencies (16/64/256)
   - Resource utilization: GPU % / memory / egress bytes (for cost estimate)

3) Timeline:
   - Bench design & scripts (today–Fri 4/16)
   - Run & analyze (Mon–Tue 4/19–4/20)
   - Package + internal QA (Wed 4/21)
   - Deliver pack + dashboard link for MAP insertion (Thu 4/22)

Action: if you confirm the prompt set and acceptance criteria (target p95 < 200ms for 128-token interactive flows, and TTFT < 120ms warm), we'll run to those targets and highlight gaps. Rafael will own the runs; Marissa will handle MAP insertion details.

Thanks — sending initial plan to Rafael now.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Customer Solutions | Redwood Inference
From: rafael.mendes@redwood.com <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Cc: Elena Torres <elena.torres@ai-analytics.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@ai-analytics.com>
Date: 2026-04-16T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff / performance checklist — bench design

Team / Elena,

Attached is the test matrix I've drafted (see RDW_MAP_v2.pdf attached to this thread). Highlights:

- Workload buckets: Dev (1–4 rps), Pre-prod (10–40 rps), Prod (100–400 rps) mapped to concurrencies 16/64/256.
- Prompts: 3 canonical templates (short dialog, doc summarization ~800 tokens, retrieval+serve ~1k tokens).
- Measurement windows: 15-minute steady-state windows per load point, three repetitions (to estimate variance).
- TTFT methodology: measure on cold worker allocation (first request after idle 20m) and warm (steady state).
- Failure & fallback tests: simulate a model variant fallback and confirm graceful degradation in MAP readout.

I'll kick off runs Monday (4/19) 06:00 UTC and stream live logs to the dashboard. We will export CSVs with the following columns: test_id, prompt_type, concurrency, requests_per_sec, tokens_per_sec, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, ttft_cold_ms, ttft_warm_ms, gpu_util_pct.

Rafael
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@ai-analytics.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@ai-analytics.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com, rafael.mendes@redwood.com
Date: 2026-04-21T17:09:00-07:00
Subject: Benchmark pack — preliminary results + packaging plan

Elena / Samir —

Delivering a short preview before tomorrow's package drop. Key highlights from the runs (prod bucket / 1024-token prompts):

- Throughput: sustained 18.2k tokens/sec at concurrency 256 (avg across 3 runs)
- Latency (1024 tokens): p50=78ms, p95=215ms, p99=391ms
- TTFT: cold=430ms, warm=95ms (warm meets your <120ms target; cold is expected due to model loading)
- Tail behavior: p99 jumps ~2.3x under model-variant fallback (we include mitigation notes)
- GPU util: 84% avg during steady-state; memory headroom 12%

Packaging plan for MAP:
- exec_readout_slides_4pp.pdf — 1-slide TL;DR, 1-slide key metrics, 1-slide risk+mitigation, 1-slide recommended SLA wording
- benchmark_results_summary.csv — canonical numbers (see columns in Rafael's note)
- raw_benchmark_logs.zip — full logs for replay (S3 link in dashboard)
- dashboard link: https://dash.redwood.ai/boards/RDW-7892/perf (interactive; CSV export button)

We'll hand the full bundle to you tomorrow (Thu 4/22) morning. If you want a 15-minute executive readout for your CTO/Procurement, we can schedule it Thu afternoon.

Karthik
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@ai-analytics.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com, rafael.mendes@redwood.com, Samir Patel <samir.patel@ai-analytics.com>

Subject: Re: Benchmark pack — preliminary results + packaging plan

Thanks — this looks great and exactly the level of detail we need. Please go ahead and:

1) Drop the bundle in the MAP today and paste the dashboard link into the "Performance benchmarks" section.
2) Send the exec_readout_slides_4pp.pdf to our CIO (c.c. Samir) with the short TL;DR you mentioned.
3) Include a short suggested SLA blurb for our legal team (Marissa will paste into procurement).

Samir — I'll forward the slides you requested to review pre-brief. Rafael / Karthik — appreciate the fast turnaround.

Best,
Elena
